input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, the conclusion remains SUPPORTED.

H1 (Restatements/Reclassifications): The retrieved evidence (E10, E11, E12) contains comprehensive income statements and other financial data but no indication of any restatement, reclassification, or correction affecting YouTube advertising revenue figures for Q2 2025 or Q2 2026. No relevant evidence was found to support this challenge.

H2 (Non-advertising components or accounting changes): The evidence actually refutes this challenge. E13 and E14 clearly distinguish between "YouTube ads" (advertising revenues) and "Google subscriptions, platforms, and devices" which includes "consumer subscriptions, which primarily include revenues from YouTube services, such as YouTube TV, YouTube Music and Premium." This confirms that YouTube advertising revenues are reported separately from YouTube subscription revenues, and there is no indication of accounting changes, acquisitions, or one-time items affecting the YouTube ads line item.

H3 (Currency effects): While E16, E17, and E18 discuss foreign currency risks and hedging activities generally, and E18 mentions that "Google subscriptions, platforms, and devices revenues were favorably affected by changes in foreign currency exchange rates," there is no specific disclosure about currency impacts on YouTube advertising revenues for Q2 2026. No relevant evidence was found.

The original calculation stands: YouTube ads revenue grew from $9,796 million (Q2 2025) to $11,055 million (Q2 2026), representing 12.86% year-over-year growth, which exceeds the 10% threshold stated in the claim.
